status: opt-in dogfood; default parallelism remains disabled
scope: Full build including preparation, hashing, TaskGroup native workers, replay/finalization and output. Native compilation cache is primed; guest parsed-source caches isolated per cold/warm pair. Process-tree RSS sum sampled at 25ms, shared mappings may be counted twice. No concurrent local tests or source mutations. Config a=ordinary whole compile (reported separately), d=same compiler image serial split control, b=TaskGroup1, c=TaskGroup2. Byte-equivalence is required for b/c/d; whole/split layout can differ and is checked by execution separately. Preparations/replays within each candidate build share its cache as they do in production.

configs.d: serial split in the same build image

limitations: Whole and split lanes have different Wasm layout; byte-equivalence is enforced across d/b/c, whole/split compiler outputs were both executed successfully.
The build still prepares twice. Completed encoded products are loaded by replay and are not bounded by the dispatch wave limit.
RC .vibe core builds only; explicit VIBE_UNSTABLE=1 and VIBE_TASKGROUP_LOWERING=1; installed-toolchain packaging and minify are unsupported.
TaskGroup is slower than the ordinary compiler and serial split. SIMD improves the new route, not the default compiler.
RSS is a sampled process-tree sum and may double-count shared mappings; it is not allocation volume.
